cards.explanation: The answer is God alone. Measuring the waters in a hand, spanning the heavens and weighing mountains on a scale is a job with one name on it. The prophet asks the questions, and nobody else steps forward. I can't even weigh a cookie box without it tipping over, friends, so I'll leave the mountains to God.

The answer is False. The prophet asks who taught God the paths of justice and who showed Him the way of understanding, and no hand goes up. God didn't need a teacher. I needed three tries and a very patient Mother Miller to learn how to lift a cookie straight.

The answer is like a drop in a bucket. The prophet says the nations are like a drop in a bucket, a speck of dust on the scales. That's a very small drop next to a very big God, friends. Nobody notices one drop when the bucket is full.

The answer is False. The prophet says Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering. Lebanon was famous for its cedars (1 Kings 5:6). Even that whole forest falls short, bakers, and my little oven would give up long before it did.

The answer is wood that will not rot. The one who can't afford gold and silver chooses wood that will not rot, and then he goes looking for a skilled craftsman. That's a lot of planning for something that has to be set up by hand.

The answer is True. The text says he seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple. So he's out looking for an expert to keep his idol standing, friends. That's a lot of effort for something that needs help standing.

The answer is above the circle of the earth. The prophet says He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth. That's a seat above the whole circle, not down in it, bakers. Quite the view, if you ask me.

The answer is grasshoppers. The prophet says God sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its dwellers are like grasshoppers. That's a small, hopping comparison, friends. Nobody down here is looking down on anybody.

The answer is stubble. A whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble. Those are the dry leftovers after a harvest, and a whirlwind carries them off without any trouble. That's how easily the rulers of the earth are swept away, friends.

The answer is that He calls each one by name. He leads forth the starry host by number and calls each one by name. Every star is counted and every star has a name, bakers. I named six cookie cutter kids and six toppings, and that was plenty of work.

The answer is True. The prophet says that because of God's great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing. Every star is accounted for, friends. The reason he gives is His power and strength.

The answer is that their way is hidden from Him. Jacob and Israel say, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God…” That's their complaint, and the prophet answers it right away. I know that feeling a little, friends. I sat in a junk drawer for years thinking nobody remembered me.
The answer is False. The everlasting God will not grow tired or weary. I get tired after one batch, bakers, and my mustache gets tired before I do. He doesn't.

The answer is that no one can search it out. The prophet says His understanding is beyond searching out. You can dig as long as you like and never reach the bottom, friends. That's a good thing to know when you don't understand His ways.
The answer is faint. The LORD gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak. He gives to the ones who are running out, bakers. I know a few mornings like that.

The answer is those who wait upon the LORD. Those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength. Even the strong grow tired, friends, so waiting on Him is the way. I'm still learning that one, since I've never been good at waiting for the oven timer.
The answer is True. Those who wait upon the LORD will run and not grow weary. Picture a run with no weariness at the end, bakers. That's more than I manage on my best day.
